tagline: AI thumbnail generator for YouTube creators.
verdictSummary: A personal thumbnail generator — a style picker, a generated background composited with your own photo, a bold text layer — is a real weekend build wrapping an image-generation API. What doesn't come with it is ThumblifyAI's actual product: prompts tuned specifically for what makes a thumbnail get clicked, refined continuously against real performance.
coreLoopDIY: Generate a background image from a title and style preset, composite an uploaded photo onto it, and add a bold text layer — producing a few variants to choose from.
whatYouLose: thumbnail-specific prompt tuning refined over time
a workflow built specifically around a creator's process
whyPeopleStillPay: The value isn't image generation itself — it's not having to become a prompt expert to get a thumbnail that actually gets clicks. People pay for a tuned, fast, repeatable path from an idea to a finished thumbnail.
notes: A straightforward, well-scoped entry: the generation mechanics are easy, the tuning behind what makes a thumbnail click-worthy is the part that took real iteration.
prompt:
Build a personal YouTube thumbnail generator: take a video title, an uploaded photo of yourself or the subject, and a style preset (a handful of common thumbnail styles cover most cases) as input. Generate a background image from the title and style through an image-generation API, then composite the uploaded photo onto it — cut the subject out with a local background-removal tool, add a drop shadow and rim light so it reads as intentional, not pasted. Render a bold text layer over the composite: either the title itself or a short, punchier hook suggested by an LLM, in a heavy outlined font. Output the final image at standard YouTube thumbnail dimensions, along with a few variants to choose between. Save every generation with the exact prompt and settings used, so a style is repeatable later, and keep a history page for one-click re-runs.

Do not build accounts, team features, or A/B testing against real YouTube performance — this generates one thumbnail at a time for your own channel, and that's the honest, complete scope.

faq.q: Can I import my existing ThumblifyAI thumbnails?
faq.a: The images themselves, yes, if you've saved them — they're just files. The specific prompts and style tuning behind them aren't exported, so recreating a look means starting a new prompt.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: Uploading a photo and picking a style works on a phone browser, but reviewing and comparing generated variants is easier on a larger screen.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Image-generation API usage per thumbnail, typically a small amount per image — hosting the small app itself is close to free.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Prompts tuned for clicks specifically. ThumblifyAI's actual edge is prompt and workflow tuning refined against what makes people click, not the ability to generate an image — this build gives you a solid starting point, not that accumulated tuning.
